GRUB is a boot loader, it just starts the boot sequence of the selected OS. The Xubuntu installer allows installing besides an existing OS and shrinking their partitions with some file systems, I don't know about win10 though. It's probably easiest to install win first without using the whole disk and then Xubuntu.

That's what I was thinking, set up a partition for each OS. I dualbooted Ubuntu and Win in the past a couple of times, with XP, Win7, even Win8, but I'm not sure how Win10 will handle things. I'll try it probably next week, right now I'm copying my files to an external HDD.

Yea it is. I tried it out and it worked fine. I also updated a Win7/Xubuntu dual boot and had no issues with the Win10 upgrade overwriting Grub bootloader.

Edit: And yes install Windows first as it likes to overwrite the Xubuntu/Grub bootloader on a clean install.
If you're going to dual-boot, always install Windows first. From my experience, windows bootloader wont tolerate any other OS' bootloader.
